title: Role-Based Access Control for AI Agents
summary: Agentic Fabriq is the identity and permissioning layer for AI agents. Per-agent identity, least-privilege access, full audit logs, and one-click revocation across MCP, OAuth, and agent frameworks. Drop-in with Okta, Azure AD, and Google Workspace.
body_text: Overview Once an enterprise decides that agents should be governed, the first practical question is how to express what each agent is allowed to do. Role-based access control is the natural place to start. It is the model most security teams already know, already operate, and already trust for human users. RBAC translates cleanly to agents, and it solves a real problem: it gives autonomy a standardized, reviewable shape instead of a tangle of one-off permissions. But agents are not static employees with a fixed desk and a fixed scope. They act on behalf of different users, across different data, in different situations, often many times a minute. That is where roles alone start to strain. This post covers what RBAC does well for agents, exactly where it runs out of room, and how to combine it with policy so that an agent has both a role and a set of boundaries . What RBAC Means for Agents Role-based access control is an authorization model where permissions are grouped into named roles, and roles are assigned to actors. Instead of granting each capability individually, you define a role once and attach it to anything that should behave that way. For agents, a role becomes a reusable bundle of permissions that maps to a recognizable job. A few concrete shapes: An IT operations triage agent can read alerts, acknowledge incidents, and post status updates to a channel — but it cannot restart production services on its own. A data analytics agent can run read-only queries against the warehouse and generate dashboards, but it cannot write to source tables or export raw records outside the environment. A procurement assistant can read the vendor catalog, draft purchase requests, and check budget remaining — but it cannot approve a purchase order. The pattern is the same in each case: the role describes the kind of work, and the permissions describe the verbs that work involves. An agent assigned the analytics-readonly role inherits a known set of capabilities, and you reason about it as a category rather than as a unique snowflake. Why RBAC Works as a Foundation RBAC earns its place because it makes agent permissions standardized, legible, and reviewable — three properties that are hard to retrofit once permissions sprawl. The value shows up most clearly in how different teams interact with the same role: Security teams approve a role once and reuse it across every agent of that type. They review the shape of access, not a hundred individual grants. Business teams can understand what an agent is allowed to do without reading a permission manifest. The role name carries meaning. Compliance teams can check whether the permissions actually match the agent's stated purpose — a role called finance-reporting that quietly includes write access to ledgers is an obvious red flag. Roles also scale operationally. When you deploy your tenth analytics agent, you do not negotiate its permissions from scratch — you attach the existing role and move on. Tightening a permission later means editing one role rather than chasing down every agent that happened to be granted it directly. The takeaway: RBAC turns agent authorization from a per-agent improvisation into a small set of reviewable categories. That alone removes a large class of governance failures. Where RBAC Runs Out of Room RBAC describes what kind of thing an agent can do. It is much weaker at describing when, on what, and on whose behalf . Agents constantly need those finer distinctions, because a single role often spans situations that should be treated very differently. Consider the gaps that a flat role cannot express: A marketing agent may be allowed to draft a campaign email, but not to send it to an external audience without sign-off. A legal review agent may read most contracts, but should be blocked from documents flagged as privileged or under litigation hold. An HR assistant may answer questions about a person's own records, but must not surface compensation data for employees the requesting user does not manage. A data analytics agent may query a dataset only if the user who invoked it already has access to that dataset. Each of these depends on context : the specific record, the data classification, the user's relationship to the resource, the direction of an action, or whether an approval exists. A role is a coarse instrument. To handle these cleanly with RBAC alone you would have to invent ever-narrower roles — hr-assistant-own-records , hr-assistant-direct-reports — until the role catalog explodes and stops being legible. That is the symptom that RBAC has reached its limit. Where Policy Begins The fix is not to abandon roles. It is to pair them with attribute-based access control — policy that evaluates the attributes of the request at the moment of the action. RBAC answers "is this the right kind of agent?" Policy answers "is this specific action allowed right now?" Keep the role broad and let policy add precision. An agent might hold the role customer-support , while policies further constrain it based on customer region, ticket sensitivity, the invoking user's group, approval status, or the type of action being attempted. A policy for the legal review agent might look like this in plain pseudocode: allow read on contract when agent.role == "legal-review" and contract.classification != "privileged" and contract.litigation_hold == false allow send on contract.summary when action.recipient == "internal" deny send on contract.summary when action.recipient == "external" and approval.status != "granted" The role still does the heavy lifting of saying "this is a legal review agent." The policy layer captures the conditions that change from request to request — classification, hold status, recipient, approval. Crucially, these conditions are data-driven , so they hold even as new contracts and new users appear, without anyone editing a role. The Layered Model In practice the strongest approach is layered, with each layer doing the one job it is good at. None of them is sufficient alone, and none of them tries to be. • RBAC provides reusable permission bundles — the broad shape of what an agent type may do. • Policy conditions provide precision — the contextual rules that narrow a role to the specific resource, user, and situation. • Human approvals provide control for high-risk actions — the deliberate pause before something irreversible, such as releasing funds or sending an external commitment. • Audit trails provide evidence — a record of which role, which policy decision, and which approval produced a given action. Read top to bottom, the layers move from coarse to fine to accountable. The role decides the category, the policy decides the instance, the approval decides the exception, and the audit trail proves what happened. A high-risk procurement action, for example, passes through all four: the procurement role permits drafting, a policy checks that the amount is within a threshold and the budget exists, an approval gate stops anything above the threshold, and the audit trail captures the whole chain. In Practice Putting this together does not require a rewrite. It requires deciding which decisions belong in roles and which belong in policy — and resisting the temptation to encode everything as a new role. A useful rule of thumb when designing agent authorization: If a permission is stable and tied to the agent's purpose , it belongs in the role. "Can read the warehouse" is a role decision. If a permission depends on the specific request — which record, which user, which classification, which threshold — it belongs in policy. "Can read this dataset because the caller can" is a policy decision. If an action is irreversible or externally visible , route it through an approval regardless of role and policy. Whatever the layers decide, write the decision and its inputs to an audit trail so it can be reviewed later. The common failure mode is the opposite: teams overload roles with situational logic, end up with hundreds of nearly identical roles, and lose the legibility that made RBAC valuable in the first place. Keep roles few and broad. Push the "it depends" into policy, where it belongs. Roles and Boundaries For enterprises scaling AI agents, RBAC is a strong foundation — but it should not be the entire authorization strategy. Roles give agents a recognizable identity and a reviewable scope. They do not, by themselves, capture the context that determines whether a single action is actually safe in the moment. The answer is to treat authorization as layers that compose: roles for the broad shape, policy for precision, approvals for the high-risk edges, and audit trails for evidence. Each is simple on its own; together they let an agent act with autonomy that is still bounded and accountable. Agents need roles, but they also need boundaries. RBAC defines the role. Policy, approvals, and audit define the boundary — and an enterprise needs all of them to let agents act safely at scale.

title: 3D Systems Enables First FDA Clearance for Implant from a Point-of-Care Institution
summary:
3D Systems Enables First FDA Clearance for Implant from a Point-of-Care Institution Elizabeth Piet Mon, 07/27/2026 - 14:00
Release Date
Tuesday, Jul 28, 2026 7:00 AM
  • Collaboration with Defense Health Agency (DHA) enables Walter Reed 3D Medical Application Center (3D MAC) to achieve first FDA-cleared medical device 
  • First-ever FDA clearance for an implant granted to a point-of-care institution
  • Reinforces 3D Systems’ leadership in guiding healthcare partners from concept to regulatory clearance and commercialization of 3D-printed, patient-specific devices

ROCK HILL, South Carolina, July 28, 2026 – Today, 3D Systems (NYSE: DDD) announced its role in enabling the Defense Health Agency (DHA) and the Walter Reed National Military Medical Center’s 3D Medical Applications Center (3D MAC) to achieve U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) premarket clearance for the 3D MAC Titanium Cranial Plate (TCP) System, the first-ever FDA-cleared implant granted to a point-of-care institution. 3D MAC's patient-specific Titanium Cranial Plate (TCP) will be used to treat U.S. active duty personnel and war fighters suffering from traumatic head injuries around the world. 

Advancing Point-of-Care Manufacturing Through Collaboration

This milestone represents the culmination of a multi-year collaboration between 3D Systems and 3D MAC to advance additive manufacturing in clinical environments. The 3D Medical Applications Center, based at Walter Reed National Military Medical Center, specializes in patient-specific anatomical models, surgical guides, and implants to support personalized care for service members and veterans.

“We believe point-of-care manufacturing is transforming the future of healthcare by bringing personalized medical devices closer to the patient. Our unique collaborations with the U.S. Defense Health Agency and the Department of Veterans Affairs underscore our leadership in this space and reinforce our commitment to expanding this business as a long-term growth driver for 3D Systems." said Jeff Graves, President and CEO of 3D Systems. Throughout the engagement, 3D Systems worked closely with 3D MAC to establish a robust quality management system (QMS) and provided support across the full development lifecycle, from design and validation through regulatory submission. The FDA clearance of the Titanium Cranial Plate System marks 3D MAC’s first-ever FDA-cleared medical device.

Enabling Regulatory Readiness and Clinical Innovation

3D Systems provided expertise in process controls, device design optimization, additive manufacturing workflows, and regulatory strategy to support 3D MAC in achieving premarket clearance. This collaboration enabled the transition from concept to an FDA-cleared implant manufactured at the point-of-care.

Natalie Byrnes, Manager of Product Development - Patient Specific Medical Technology, 3D Systems said “This clearance underscores the power of combining clinical innovation with deep expertise in additive manufacturing and regulatory compliance. We are honored to help enable expanded access to personalized care delivered at the point of treatment.”

Industry Leadership and Future Opportunities

The clearance establishes multiple industry firsts, including the first FDA-cleared implant granted to a point-of-care institution and 3D MAC’s first FDA-cleared medical device. It reinforces 3D Systems’ leadership in enabling point-of-care manufacturing and highlights its ability to help healthcare institutions navigate the path from concept through regulatory clearance and commercialization.

This achievement further strengthens 3D Systems’ relationships with the Defense Health Agency and the Department of Veterans Affairs and positions the company to support future initiatives in advanced, patient-specific medical manufacturing.

The clearance is listed on the FDA website under submission number K253116.

About 3D Systems

For 40 years Chuck Hull’s curiosity and desire to improve the way products were designed and manufactured gave birth to 3D printing, 3D Systems, and the additive manufacturing industry. Since then, that same spark continues to ignite the 3D Systems team as we work side-by-side with our customers to change the way industries innovate. As a full-service solutions partner, we deliver industry-leading 3D printing technologies, materials and software to high-value markets such as medical and dental; aerospace, space and defense; transportation and motorsports; AI infrastructure; and durable goods. Each application-specific solution is powered by the expertise and passion of our employees who endeavor to achieve our shared goal of Transforming Manufacturing for a Better Future. More information on the company is available at www.3dsystems.com.

title: Noetra Launches Full-Scale R&D for Japan-Developed Multimodal Foundation Model
summary: Honda Global | Noetra Corp., along with its core member companies and investors—Sony Group Corporation, SoftBank Corp., NEC Corporation, and Honda Motor Co., Ltd.—launched full-scale R&D for a Japan-developed multimodal foundation model that will serve as the foundation for AI-enabled robots and physical AI, in collaboration with a broad range of partners engaged in the development and application of sovereign AI in Japan.
body_text: Noetra Corp. Sony Group Corporation SoftBank Corp. NEC Corporation Honda Motor Co., Ltd. Noetra Corp., along with its core member companies and investors—Sony Group Corporation, SoftBank Corp., NEC Corporation, and Honda Motor Co., Ltd.—launched full-scale R&D for a Japan-developed multimodal foundation model that will serve as the foundation for AI-enabled robots and physical AI, in collaboration with a broad range of partners engaged in the development and application of sovereign AI in Japan. Noetra has received investments from a total of 44 companies and organizations, including enterprises engaged in the development of sovereign AI and companies across a wide range of industries, led by the manufacturing sector, that are promoting AI adoption, all of which share Noetra's vision and business strategy. For the development of its homegrown multimodal foundation model, Noetra established a research and development organization centered on engineers seconded from its core member companies and investors, the National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Preferred Networks, Inc., and other participating organizations. By leveraging the technologies and expertise these organizations have cultivated through AI model development, Noetra will accelerate its R&D initiatives. Noetra will begin developing its homegrown multimodal foundation model by leveraging AI computing infrastructure operated by Japan-based providers. To accelerate development of the model, in collaboration with NVIDIA, Noetra also plans to build AI computing infrastructure equipped with approximately 27,500 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs, NVIDIA's latest graphics processing units (GPUs) optimized for agentic AI workloads centered on large-scale foundation models. Construction is scheduled to begin in April 2027, with operations expected to begin in June 2028. Starting in phases from the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027 (fiscal 2026), Noetra aims to build a reasoning foundation model that will serve as the core of AI agents and natural language processing, equipped with foundational capabilities such as advanced Japanese language understanding, logical reasoning, and instruction following. By fiscal 2028, Noetra plans to develop an omni-modal foundation model capable of seamlessly processing text, images, video and audio, with the goal of realizing AI that can understand and leverage diverse data across modalities. Looking ahead to fiscal 2030, Noetra will pursue the realization of “Real-world Native AI” capable of understanding physical properties such as spatial awareness and designed for deployment in real-world environments. The models developed by Noetra will be made available externally and released in stages, factoring in R&D progress as well as real-world implementation. Hironobu Tamba, President and CEO, Noetra Corp., commented as follows: “For Japan to become a global leader in physical AI, it is essential to develop multimodal foundation models that will strengthen the nation's industrial competitiveness while helping address societal challenges and creating new value. Working together with our partners, Noetra will build these multimodal foundation models while striving to realize trusted AI infrastructure that supports the transformation of Japan's industries and society.” Hiroki Totoki, President and CEO, Sony Group Corporation, commented as follows: “The development of a multimodal foundation model in Japan is an important initiative that will strengthen Japan’s capabilities in the field of physical AI and accelerate its real-world deployment. We consider it highly meaningful for Sony to participate in this initiative as one of its core member companies. Going forward, we intend to leverage the knowledge and insights gained through the joint development of this foundation model not only in the area of entertainment, but also in semiconductors, which play a critical role in physical AI. By collaborating with a diverse range of partners, we aim to contribute to the creation of new value.” Junichi Miyakawa, President & CEO, SoftBank Corp., commented as follows: “In a society that coexists with AI, the data held by Japan's industries and businesses will be a key source of competitive strength. Creating an environment in which that data can be securely utilized within Japan is essential to strengthening the country's industrial competitiveness. We expect Noetra to play a central role in building that environment. As a core member, we will support Noetra's efforts by providing AI infrastructure and other resources, while working closely with Noetra and our fellow partners to drive the growth of Japan's industries and foster innovation.” Takayuki Morita, President and CEO, NEC Corporation, commented as follows: “NEC is one of the few companies in Japan capable of providing end-to-end AI development—from building foundation models entirely from scratch to system implementation and operation. Leveraging our expertise and technologies, NEC will contribute to the development of Noetra's domestically produced multimodal foundation models. Building upon this foundation, we will accelerate the development and real-world deployment of specialized AI models that power advanced services, including those for physical AI. As AI is increasingly utilized across every facet of society, developing unique Japanese models and expanding options through collaboration among various companies is critical, particularly from the perspective of economic security. By turning Japan's renowned know-how and high-quality physical data into value, NEC is helping to strengthen Japan's competitiveness in the AI-driven industrial revolution.” Toshihiro Mibe, Director, President and Representative Executive Officer, Honda Motor Co., Ltd., commented as follows: “Since its founding, Honda has embraced the philosophy of 'Technology for People,' continually taking on new challenges to expand the possibilities of people's lives and mobility. We also believe AI is a technology that can help address challenges people and society are facing. Realizing AI’s potential requires collaboration with a diverse range of companies and research institutions. By leveraging the technologies and expertise we have cultivated through decades of manufacturing, we aim to accelerate the real-world deployment of technologies born from our collaboration through Noetra and contribute to solving societal challenges and creating new value in fields, including mobility and robotics.” Major participating companies (in alphabetical order) Asahi Kasei Corporation DAIICHI SANKYO COMPANY, LIMITED DAIKIN INDUSTRIES, LTD. title: Why radiopharmaceuticals: Scientific promise meets market momentum
body_text: While scientific promise of radiopharmaceuticals is widely recognized, what often goes underappreciated is how fundamentally they reshape not just treatment approaches, but the way clinical trials are designed and executed. In the first episode of Radiopharmaceutical Trials: The Playbook, Hector Herrero (Senior Director, Global Radiopharmaceutical Management, Fortrea) is joined by Dr. Ravi Karra (GE Healthcare) and Dr. Paulo Nunes (Fortrea) to unpack the drivers behind this momentum, and the operational realities that come with it A turning point in oncology Radiopharmaceuticals are not new. Therapies like radioactive iodine have been used for decades. However, the field is now at an inflection point, driven by the rise of theranostics —a precision medicine approach that combines targeted diagnostics with targeted therapy. Several factors are fueling this resurgence: A growing number of biological targets (e.g., PSMA, SSTR2, FAP) Advances in isotope production and supply chain capabilities Expansion into new indications, including earlier lines of therapy and combination approaches Together, these advances are accelerating clinical development and positioning radiopharmaceuticals as a key modality across multiple solid tumors. Beyond a drug: A complex modality Radiopharmaceuticals are unique in that they combine a targeting molecule with a radioactive payload, enabling highly precise delivery of radiation to tumors while minimizing exposure to healthy tissue. This dual nature makes them powerful, but also introduces significant complexity, particularly in clinical trials. Unlike traditional oncology studies, radiopharmaceutical trials require: Specialized infrastructure (nuclear medicine, radiopharmacy) Cross-functional collaboration across departments Highly trained staff familiar with radiation handling and safety This creates an additional layer of coordination that many sites are not yet fully equipped to manage. The critical role of logistics If there is one defining feature of radiopharmaceutical trials, it is the importance of timing. Many of these therapies rely on isotopes with short half-lives, meaning production, delivery and administration must be precisely coordinated. There is no “off-the-shelf” model, manufacturing often begins only once a patient is scheduled. Any disruption, whether in production, quality control or transport, can result in missed treatment opportunities. This makes radiopharmaceutical trials among the most operationally intensive in clinical research, requiring seamless coordination across sponsors, CROs, sites, manufacturers and logistics providers. Operational complexity at every step From regulatory requirements to site readiness, radiopharmaceutical trials demand a more rigorous and integrated approach. Key considerations include: Country-specific radiation protection regulations Stringent quality control from production to administration Imaging standardization across sites Compliance with companion diagnostic regulations These requirements can extend study timelines and limit participation to highly specialized centers, though efforts are underway to expand capabilities more broadly. Keeping the patient at the center Amid this complexity, the patient experience remains paramount. Scheduling is not just about clinic availability, it depends on a tightly aligned chain of events, from isotope production to staff readiness. When disruptions occur, the impact goes beyond timelines and costs. Delays or cancellations can affect patient confidence, site morale and overall trial engagement highlighting the need for reliability and precision at every step. Innovation requires a new mindset Radiopharmaceuticals represent more than a scientific breakthrough, they demand operational excellence. Success in this space depends on understanding the full ecosystem and ensuring every component works in sync. As the series continues, future episodes will explore how to select the right sites, optimize logistics and navigate common operational challenges. Radiopharmaceuticals hold immense potential. Realizing that opportunity, however, requires not only innovation in science but discipline in execution. To dive deeper into the operational, clinical and strategic considerations shaping this space, explore the full Radiopharmaceutical Trials: The Playbook podcast series and stay tuned for upcoming episodes

title: Tracking Your Cycles with Inito: Understanding Your Fertility Results
summary: Learn all about tracking your cycles with Inito, including how to interpret your fertility chart, track and confirm ovulation, & decode your hormone trends.
body_text: Every menstrual cycle tells a unique story. While a menstrual cycle tracker can tell you when your period is due, one of the best ways to track your cycle is to understand how your hormones change throughout it. From your first Reference Day Test to Ovulation Confirmation, each fertility rating reflects a different stage of your cycle. In this guide, you’ll learn what each fertility rating means, how your hormones change throughout the cycle, what to expect next, and why your results may look different from one cycle to another. Whether you’re new to Inito or looking to better understand your hormone patterns, this Inito chart guide will help you make sense of every stage of your cycle. Key Takeaways Your cycle begins on Cycle Day 1, when you start your period. Your fertility ratings change as your hormones change throughout the cycle. Reference Day testing establishes your baseline for all four key fertility hormones. Low Fertility means estrogen and LH have not risen above your baseline levels. This means your fertile window has not opened yet. After Low Fertility, rising estrogen leads to High Fertility, signaling that ovulation is approaching. During High Fertility, sperm can survive up to five days, increasing your chances of conception. Inito then looks for a rise in LH to identify Peak Fertility, your most fertile moment. Peak Fertility indicates ovulation will likely occur within the next 24–36 hours. After Peak, you enter Waiting for PdG Rise, the phase between LH surge and ovulation confirmation. During the Waiting for PdG Rise phase, you are in Low Fertility again since you have crossed your fertile window, and your chances of conceiving are low. A steady increase in PdG marks Ovulation Confirmed, meaning the egg has been released. The “two-week wait” follows ovulation and is the time to focus on rest and self-care. Your chart may vary each cycle due to natural hormonal fluctuations. How does your fertility journey begin with Inito? Every cycle begins with your period: this marks Cycle Day 1, or CD 1 for short. During your period, estrogen and progesterone have fallen back to their baseline levels, allowing your body to begin preparing a new group of follicles for the next ovulation. As you log your period in the Inito app, your personalized testing schedule is created for the rest of your cycle. One of the first important milestones you’ll see is your Reference Day Test. What is a Reference Day Test? Most users start taking their Reference Day Test on Cycle Day 6 or 7 (This is marked by a blue triangle icon in your Inito calendar). These are some of the most important tests of your cycle. What does the Reference Day Test indicate? Although it may seem like just another test day, it’s actually one of the most important tests you’ll take during your cycle. On this day, Inito measures your baseline levels of: FSH (Follicle Stimulating Hormone) LH (Luteinizing Hormone) E3G (Estrogen) PdG (Urine metabolite of Progesterone) These baseline measurements allow Inito to personalize your fertility insights throughout the rest of your cycle. By understanding your starting point, Inito can: Pick up even small hormonal shifts Pinpoint your actual fertile window Detect your LH surge with accuracy Confirm ovulation through a rise in PdG Know more: A Complete Guide to Testing with the Inito Fertility Monitor Why are the Reference Day tests so important? Because every woman’s hormonal pattern is different. Your trends might be higher or lower than someone else’s and it may also shift slightly from cycle to cycle. The Reference Day Test ensures that Inito is comparing your upcoming results to your own baseline , not average thresholds. This enables more accurate tracking through the rest of your cycle. Know more: Best Time to Test with Inito for Accurate Readings What is Low Fertility in the Follicular Phase? When you first start testing, you’ll likely see Low Fertility (including on your Reference Day tests). What does Low Fertility mean? Low Fertility means your estrogen and LH levels haven’t yet risen above your baseline, so your fertile window hasn’t opened. If you’ve just started testing, seeing Low Fertility is exactly what you’d expect. In fact, it’s the result you’ll likely see most often throughout your cycle. A Low Fertility result means that your likelihood of getting pregnant is low on this day –and that’s completely okay! In fact, Low Fertility is the result you’ll see most often during your cycle. Low Fertility at this point in your cycle simply tells you: Your estrogen levels have not yet begun rising You’re still early in your follicular phase Your egg is yet to be released Note: It does not mean that anything is wrong or that your fertility is low . It is expected at the beginning of your cycle. What can I expect after Low Fertility? As one follicle becomes dominant, it begins producing more estrogen. Once estrogen rises above your personal baseline, Inito recognizes that your fertile window is opening and changes your fertility status to High Fertility . This is why continuing to test as recommended is so important. These early hormone values help Inito identify the changes that signal your fertile window is approaching. Know more: Trying to Get Pregnant? Get to Know Your Follicular Phase What is High Fertility in the Late Follicular Phase? High Fertility is your signal that your fertile window is opening. What does High Fertility mean? High Fertility means that your estrogen (E3G) levels have risen above baseline, so your body is preparing to ovulate soon. As your dominant follicle grows, it produces increasing amounts of estrogen. Estrogen typically starts to rise about 3-4 days before the release of the egg. Unlike LH-only tests that typically identify only the day or two before ovulation, rising estrogen allows Inito to pinpoint your fertile window, giving you more opportunities to try on the right days before the egg is released. Know more: Estradiol Levels Chart: Tracking Estrogen Levels What does High Fertility mean in my TTC journey? Estrogen doesn’t just prepare the follicle–it also creates conditions that support conception. During this time: Cervical mucus becomes more sperm-friendly. Sperm can survive for up to five days. Your chances of conception begin increasing. For couples trying to conceive, this is an ideal time to have intercourse every day or every other day. What can I expect after High Fertility? After estrogen has risen, Inito begins watching for a rise in your LH levels. Once LH rises above your baseline, you’ll receive Peak Fertility , signaling that ovulation is likely to occur within the next 24-36 hours. So, it’s important to keep testing as and when the app suggests to make sure you don’t miss it. Catching your LH peak is key to identifying your most fertile moment of the cycle. What does Peak Fertility Mean in My Cycle? Peak Fertility is when the chances of pregnancy are the highest in your cycle. What does Peak Fertility mean? Peak Fertility means Inito has detected an LH surge, indicating that ovulation may occur within the next 24-36 hours. The LH surge is one of the most important hormonal events of your cycle. When LH rises, it triggers the dominant follicle to release the mature egg, a process known as ovulation. This helps you track ovulation with confidence instead of relying on calendar estimates alone. Know more: How Does LH Surge Impact Ovulation? What does Peak Fertility mean in my TTC journey? Peak Fertility represents your highest chance of conception during that cycle. The egg survives for only up to 24 hours after release , so this is one of the best times to have intercourse. This ensures that the sperm are already waiting in the reproductive tract when ovulation occurs. Know more: What are Your Chances of Getting Pregnant on Ovulation Day? What can I expect next? Although an LH surge predicts that ovulation is about to happen, it doesn’t actually confirm that the egg has been released. That’s why Inito asks you to keep testing after Peak Fertility. In the next stage of your cycle, Inito looks for a sustained rise in PdG, the urine metabolite of progesterone, to confirm ovulation. Waiting for PdG Rise: How Is It Related to Ovulation Confirmation? After Peak Fertility, you’ll notice that Inito shows you a result called Waiting for PdG Rise. What does Waiting for PdG Rise mean? This is the time between your Peak Fertility and Ovulation Confirmation. After ovulation, the ruptured follicle transforms into the corpus luteum , which begins producing progesterone. When progesterone increases, PdG (the urine metabolite of progesterone) rises as well. A steady and consistent PdG rise confirms that ovulation has actually taken place–and this is exactly what Inito looks for to mark Ovulation Confirmed . What does Waiting for PdG Rise mean in my TTC journey? At this point, your body has done the work needed to support ovulation. This means: Your fertile window has likely closed (unless you see another LH surge). Your body is transitioning into the luteal phase. Inito is tracking your PdG to confirm that ovulation has occurred by tracking your PdG. What can I expect next? One of two things may happen: Ovulation Confirmation: Once your PdG levels show a sustained rise in the days following your LH surge, you’ll receive an Ovulation Confirmed result. Another LH surge: If PdG doesn’t rise, you may experience another LH surge before ovulation occurs. This is why Inito continues asking you to test after Peak Fertility—it helps capture both ovulation confirmation and any additional LH surges that may occur. Know more: PdG Results on Inito Explained: Waiting for Rise, Rising, Confirmed, or Unlikely? What does Ovulation Confirmed Mean in my Cycle? Short answer: Ovulation Confirmed means Inito has detected a steady and consistent PdG rise after your LH surge, indicating that ovulation has likely occurred. Receiving an Ovulation Confirmed result is an important milestone because it means your hormone pattern is consistent with ovulation having taken place. Unlike LH, which predicts ovulation, PdG provides confirmation that your body has responded to the LH surge and released the egg. When did I ovulate? Since ovulation typically occurs 24-36 hours after your true LH surge, Inito marks your Ovulation day as Peak Fertility day + 1. This means, If the latest Peak Fertility was detected on CD16 , Your ovulation day = CD17 What can I expect next? Entering the luteal phase: After ovulation, your body shifts into the luteal phase. During this phase, progesterone remains elevated to help support the uterine lining in case pregnancy occurs. Do I need to keep testing? Further testing isn’t required after ovulation has been confirmed. However, some people like to continue tracking to monitor their overall cycle patterns. The two-week wait: The stretch between ovulation and your next period (or a positive pregnancy test) is often called the two-week wait . It can feel long and emotionally charged, so be gentle with yourself. This is the perfect time to focus on rest, nourishment, and self-care. Know more: Your Complete Guide to Surviving the Two-Week Wait How do you calculate DPO on Inito? DPO (Days Past Ovulation) tells you how many days have passed since you ovulated. DPO is one of the most useful metrics for fertility charting because it helps you understand where you are after ovulation. Once your PdG has risen steadily after your LH surge, Inito marks the day after Peak Fertility as your Ovulation Day (0 DPO). Each day after that increases your DPO by one. Example: Peak Fertility: CD 15 – December 11 Ovulation (0 DPO): CD 16 – December 12 1 DPO: CD 17 – December 13 2 DPO: CD 18 – December 14, and so on. Note: Inito shows your DPO on the chart only after ovulation is confirmed. Putting It All Together: How Does Inito Help You Track Your Menstrual Cycle? This is how your menstrual cycle tracking looks in the Inito app during a typical ovulatory cycle: Where you are in your cycle What’s happening What you see on Inito What happens next Period (CD 1) Hormone levels reset, and a new menstrual cycle begins. Period logged in the app Follow your personalized testing schedule Reference Day Test Measuring your baseline hormone levels Reference Day Test Inito uses this baseline to personalize your fertility insights Early follicular phase Follicles begin growing, estrogen yet to rise Low Fertility Continue testing to track estrogen rise Late follicular phase Estrogen rises as the dominant follicle matures High Fertility Inito starts monitoring for your LH surge Ovulation LH surges, triggering the release of the egg Peak Fertility Continue testing so Inito can look for a PdG rise to confirm if ovulation actually happened Post-Peak Fertility Progesterone begins rising after ovulation. Waiting for PdG Rise Inito checks for a sustained PdG rise to confirm ovulation Luteal phase Ovulation has been confirmed Ovulation Confirmed Your body has done its job! Take it easy, rest, hydrate, and wait until after 12-14 DPO to take a pregnancy test Why Does My Chart Look Different? Cycles can vary from month to month, which means your hormone patterns (and the fertility results you see in Inito) may also look different. Here are some of the most common variations you might notice: 1. Why didn’t I get Peak Fertility after several days of High Fertility? Seeing multiple days of High Fertility without moving into Peak Fertility can happen for a few reasons: Early estrogen rise. Your estrogen may have risen earlier than usual, while your LH surge is still on the way. This can lead to an extended High Fertility phase before Peak Fertility. Your LH didn’t rise enough. Your LH surge may not have been strong enough to register as Peak Fertility. Hormone patterns can vary from cycle to cycle, and sometimes the surge is smaller or delayed. A rapid LH surge. LH can sometimes surge and fall within just 2-6 hours. If testing didn’t align with that brief window, you may have missed the surge. Gaps in testing . Skipping tests during your fertile window can create gaps in your hormone data, making it harder for Inito to identify a rapid rise in LH. Consistent testing is key to catching your Peak Fertility. What to do next: Keep testing. Follow the testing schedule as per the Inito app. Staying consistent increases the chances of catching important hormonal shifts. Know more: Can You Ovulate With No LH Surge? 2. Why did I go straight from Low Fertility to Peak Fertility? This can happen if: Your estrogen didn’t show a significant rise. If your estrogen levels didn’t rise much from your baseline levels, you may not get a High Fertility result. Your LH surged earlier than expected . If you had an earlier LH surge, you may jump straight to Peak Fertility without getting High Fertility. Missed tests. If you skipped a few tests in the beginning, your fertility ratings may be affected. What it means: Your body simply moved into its fertile window faster than usual. The Peak Fertility result is accurate and still indicates ovulation is approaching. Know more: Early Ovulation: Symptoms, Causes, Treatment, and More 3. “I got another Peak Fertility.” More than one LH surge occurs in over half of cycles , and this can happen because: You naturally have a multiple LH surge pattern The first LH rise wasn’t strong enough Your body attempted ovulation, but didn’t release the egg During this time, it’s helpful to continue trying to conceive, as your fertile window may still be open. Which Peak is real? The Peak Fertility that is followed by a PdG rise is your true ovulatory surge. What it means: If the second LH surge successfully triggers ovulation, your PdG levels will begin to rise steadily in the days that follow. Once Inito detects this sustained PdG increase, you’ll receive an Ovulation Confirmed result. What to do next: Continue testing as recommended. Keep testing after Peak Fertility so Inito can track your PdG levels and help confirm ovulation. Have intercourse or inseminate during Peak Fertility . If you’re trying to conceive, this is still one of your most fertile times. Know more: False LH Surge Before The Real One 4. “I got only one day of High Fertility before Peak Fertility.” If you’re seeing fewer days of High Fertility before Peak Fertility, it could be because your estrogen took a while to rise, and was immediately followed by an LH surge. Hormone patterns can vary from cycle to cycle, so the number of High Fertility days isn’t always the same. What to do next: Continue testing as recommended. Keep testing after Peak Fertility so Inito can track your PdG levels and help confirm ovulation. Have intercourse or inseminate during Peak Fertility . If you’re trying to conceive, this is still one of your most fertile times. 5. “I got an Ovulation Unlikely result.” Seeing an Ovulation Unlikely result can be disappointing, but it simply reflects how your hormones behaved this cycle. There are a few reasons this may occur: Your LH surge may not have been able to trigger the release of an egg. Missed tests or data gaps can sometimes make it harder to clearly identify your hormone pattern. Anovulatory cycles can occur once or twice a year, even in healthy women. What to do next: Keep testing in your next cycle to get a clearer picture of your hormone trends. If you notice frequent anovulatory cycles, consider sharing your charts with your doctor for personalized guidance. Remember, having an occasional anovulatory cycle is common and does not necessarily indicate a fertility problem. Know more: Anovulation: Everything you need to know about the #1 cause of infertility Final Thoughts: From Guesswork to Clarity Once you start understanding your hormone patterns, tracking your menstrual cycle becomes much easier. Instead of guessing when you might ovulate, you can track ovulation with confidence, pinpoint your fertile window, and understand how each hormone changes throughout your cycle. FAQs How do I track my menstrual cycle? The most beginner-friendly way to track your menstrual cycle is to log the first day of every period and follow your cycle over several months. While a menstrual cycle calendar tracker can predict when your next period might begin, tracking hormone changes with the Inito Fertility Monitor provides additional insight into when your fertile window opens, when ovulation is approaching, and whether ovulation has been confirmed. What is the best way to track your fertility? The best way to track your fertility is with hormone tracking. While calendar-based apps estimate fertile days based on previous cycles, Inito measures four fertility hormones–LH, estrogen, PdG, and FSH–to identify your fertile window, predict ovulation, and confirm that ovulation has occurred. When am I most fertile? You are most fertile during your fertile window. This includes the 4 days before ovulation, the day of ovulation, and the day after ovulation. Since sperm can survive in the reproductive tract for up to five days, having intercourse during your fertile window gives you the highest chance of conception. Inito identifies this window by detecting rising estrogen and LH levels. Am I fertile 2-3 days before my period? No, that’s unlikely. 2-3 days before your period is typically part of the late luteal phase, after ovulation has already occurred. Because the egg survives for only about 12-24 hours after ovulation, the chances of pregnancy tend to be low. How can I accurately track my ovulation? The most accurate way to track ovulation at home is by monitoring hormone changes rather than relying on calendar dates alone. Inito tracks rising estrogen to identify your fertile window, detects your LH surge to predict ovulation, and measures a steady and consistent rise in PdG afterward to confirm that ovulation likely occurred. What are the benefits of cycle tracking? Cycle tracking helps you better understand your menstrual cycle, recognize changes in your hormone patterns, identify your fertile window, predict ovulation, and monitor cycle-to-cycle variation. Over time, it can also provide helpful information to discuss with your healthcare provider if you notice recurring changes. Can I get pregnant 2 days after my period? Yes, it’s possible, depending on your cycle length. If you have a shorter menstrual cycle and ovulate early, sperm can survive long enough to fertilize an egg. For example, say you have a 22-day cycle with ovulation occurring around CD 8, and your period lasts for about 5 days. So, having sex 2 days after your period would be bang in the middle of your most fertile time. n Content How do I understand my Inito test results? Your Inito test results reflect your hormone levels throughout the menstrual cycle. Rising estrogen signals the start of your fertile window, an LH surge indicates Peak Fertility, and a sustained rise in PdG confirms ovulation. Together, these hormone patterns provide a clearer picture of your cycle than relying on period dates alone. Does Inito tell me which day I ovulated? Yes. Once Inito confirms ovulation with a steady and consistent rise in PdG, it tells you which day you would’ve most likely ovulated. Since ovulation typically occurs about 24-36 hours after the LH surge, your ovulation day would be calculated as Peak Fertility day + 1.

title: Honeywell Technologies advances future-ready skills through STEM-led school transformation program
summary: Honeywell Technologies announced a key milestone under Saksham, its flagship education and skilling initiative in India, with the inauguration of its first future-ready STEM education and school transformation program.
body_text: NEW DELHI, India, July 9, 2026: Honeywell Technologies (NASDAQ: HON) today announced a key milestone under Saksham , its flagship education and skilling initiative in India, with the inauguration of its first future-ready STEM education and school transformation program. The initiative was launched by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Delhi, Smt. Rekha Gupta at Shalimar Bagh Village Government Girls Senior Secondary School . As part of the program, Honeywell Technologies aims to transform 12 government and government-aided girls' schools across the country, reaching more than 12,000 students by 2029 through interventions focused on STEM education, digital literacy, student well-being and teacher development. While the most students and teachers will be impacted in Delhi, the initiative is also being implemented across Pune, Bengaluru and Gurugram. Implemented in partnership with Ladli Foundation Trust, the intervention combines modern learning infrastructure, teacher capacity building and global exposure opportunities to help create more inclusive and future-ready learning environments for adolescent girls. Speaking at the inauguration, Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon'ble Chief Minister of Delhi , said, “It is heartening to see Shalimar Bagh Village Government Girls Senior Secondary School transformed into one of Delhi's finest government schools. With smart classrooms, a computer lab, a STEM lab and an AI-enabled toilet block for our daughters through Honeywell Technologies' Saksham initiative, this school is now setting a benchmark for future-ready learning. I sincerely thank Honeywell Technologies for its contribution to our daughters and our schools. A state can truly progress only when the government and society work together, and this collaboration is a strong example of what we can achieve together.” “Building India's future workforce starts with expanding access to quality education and providing basic infrastructure,” said Ashish Modi, President, India and Asia Pacific, Honeywell Technologies . “Through Saksham, we are bringing STEM labs, digital access and experiential learning to our young students. The intervention at Shalimar Bagh school is symbolic of our effort to expand opportunities for the students and strengthen India's pipeline of future-ready talent.” The intervention at Shalimar Bagh Village Government Girls Senior Secondary School, a key milestone in Saksham's broader school transformation effort, includes: STEM laboratories that promote hands-on science and technology learning, innovation and critical thinking. Digital ICT and computer labs equipped with computers and interactive learning tools to improve digital literacy and technology access. Smart classrooms that enhance student engagement and support technology-enabled teaching. Safe and hygienic toilets and WASH infrastructure that promote menstrual dignity, hygiene and student well-being. Awareness sessions on menstrual hygiene, nutrition, cyber safety, financial literacy, and reproductive health that help students build confidence and life skills. Training for 60 teachers on digital tools and interactive teaching methodologies to support long-term learning outcomes. A global Space Science learning opportunity , through which five students from participating schools will be selected to attend an immersive workshop at the U.S. Space & Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama. As India continues to build a technology-driven and innovation-led economy, ensuring equitable access to digital learning and STEM education remains a critical challenge. According to NITI Aayog's recent report – ‘School Education System in India’ 1 , more than one-third of schools lack access to computers or internet connectivity, while nearly seven in ten schools do not have smart classrooms. Through Saksham - focused on advancing inclusive STEM education and building future-ready skills, Honeywell Technologies is helping bridge these gaps by combining modern learning infrastructure, teacher capacity building and experiential learning opportunities, enabling students to develop the skills and confidence needed to thrive in the future workforce. Implemented through Honeywell Hometown Solutions India Foundation (HHSIF), Honeywell Technologies’ philanthropic arm in India, Saksham is creating pathways for young people to develop their skills and confidence needed to succeed in a rapidly evolving world. In Delhi, the initiative will deliver interventions across government schools in Mehrauli, Tughlakabad and Shalimar Bagh, directly benefiting nearly 5,000 students, primarily adolescent girls from underserved communities. With plans to expand to an additional government school in Janakpuri during FY2026–27, Saksham continues to advance educational equity through improved infrastructure, teacher empowerment and experiential learning opportunities. About Honeywell Hometown Solutions India Foundation Honeywell Hometown Solutions India Foundation (HHSIF) is the non-profit arm of Honeywell Technologies, dedicated to advancing corporate social responsibility initiatives across India. Its focus areas include education, humanitarian relief, and sustainable community development. In education, HHSIF leads STEM-focused skilling programs, supports research at leading institutes, and helps scale deep-science start-ups. In sustainable community development, it works to build resilient communities by strengthening healthcare infrastructure and enabling rural livelihoods, WASH initiatives, and natural resource conservation through technology-led solutions. Honeywell has also committed to planting one million trees under its Plant the Future program this decade. Since inception, HHSIF has impacted more than 6.6 million lives across 21 states. About Honeywell Technologies Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial, and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions, and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy. For more news and information on Honeywell Technologies, please visit Honeywell Technologies Newsroom . 1 https://niti.gov.in/sites/default/files/2026-05/School-Education-System-in-India.pdf

title: Exploring “green” finance offerings, part 3
summary: In this third blog, we’ll explore the relationship between green finance, ESG ratings, and artificial intelligence.
body_text: We’re continuing our discussion on emerging “green” finance offerings in this four-part blog series, with an emphasis on their proliferation and importance. In part one , we took a look at green finance and green bonds, and, in part two , we examined sustainability-linked loans (SLL) and sustainable supply chain financing (SSCF). In this third blog, we’ll explore the relationship between green finance, ESG ratings, and artificial intelligence. Leveraging the power of artificial intelligence Finance is a powerful lever for motivating businesses to become more environmentally sustainable. Banks and other financial institutions are the backbones of SSCF, and they play a key role in catalyzing awareness and driving the uptake of their newest green programs and offerings. Banks are working across their departments and business segments to improve the integration of environmental, social and governance (ESG) priorities into their core products and due diligence processes, including know your customer (KYC) processes. They’re also developing new green corporate scoring models, which blend both ESG and KYC data. The increasing deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) is helping banks with these efforts by improving ESG data analytics. The key to success is unlocking insights from data to inform sustainable investment strategies and ESG performance ratings, both in the present and over the long term. Assessing risks Rating a company’s ESG performance involves risk because ESG rating providers use different frameworks, measurements, metrics, data, and qualitative analysis. Despite their increasing use of ESG ratings over the past year, banks often lack the necessary tools to inform their ESG rating decision-making in an efficient and appropriate way. In addition, a large portion of ESG data analysis covers non-financial elements of a company’s actions related to sustainability. Research also reveals concerns about the reliability of ESG and KYC data. Frequently there are gaps in data availability, data inaccuracies, and a lack of comparability across ESG providers. As a result, ESG rating analysis and consistency is a difficult task for banks, indeed. Assessing benefits AI can enable more informed ESG rating decision-making by limiting the subjectivity and cognitive bias that may stem from traditional analysis, reducing the noise in ESG data and making use of unstructured data. Specifically, natural language processing can be used to analyze massive amounts of unstructured datasets—think geo-localization and social media—to perform sentiment analysis and identify patterns and relationships in data. The results of such analysis can be used to assign quantitative values to qualitative data for sustainability parameters. This measurable clarity represents the power of AI at its best. Alternative uses of AI In recent years, alternative ESG ratings providers have emerged, offering ratings based on AI with a view to providing a more objective, outside-in perspective of a company’s sustainability performance. Some experts predict that these alternative ESG ratings won’t replace traditional ESG ratings, but instead be used to complement existing knowledge about the buyer, supplier and customer. In fact, the use of AI could be used by rated corporations themselves to further inform their ESG decision-making and strategic direction. Additionally, using AI to generate ESG ratings could help minimize “greenwashing” by corporations by uncovering less readily available information about their sustainability practices. This might be another context in which the power of AI is particularly valuable. In our next and final blog in this series, we’ll discuss the future of green finance and how you can make the shift towards sustainability. In the meantime, if you’d like further information on this or other related topics, reach out to either of us ( nancy.amert@cgi.com ; andy.schmidt@cgi.com ).
